sample_unit: LLM responses (40 per model), each rated by 4 clinicians

links.outcome: Rated quality and demographic bias of LLM explanations when prompt patient gender and age were varied
links.effect: Mean possibility of demographic bias was 2.49 for GPT-4 and 2.93 for Gemini. GPT-4-turbo ratings were slightly higher for male than female patients on all measures except age-appropriateness. Gemini's gender differences were less pronounced.
links.quote: Ratings on all measures, with the exception of age-appropriateness, were slightly higher for responses generated for male patients as compared to female patients with GPT-4-turbo, while the gender differences were less pronounced with Gemini 1.0 Pro.

screen.reason: The study empirically assesses the accuracy, completeness, demographic bias, and age-appropriateness of off-the-shelf LLMs (GPT-4-turbo and Gemini 1.0 Pro) in generating pediatric surgical explanations using expert clinician evaluation, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or compare outcomes with/without a deployment practice.
